title: Pineapple lace shawl
subtitle: A rectangle of traditional pineapple motifs in lace-weight yarn, worked across a long foundation chain
excerpt: Pineapple crochet is a Victorian lace tradition using clusters of double trebles fanned from a chain space to form a tapered pineapple shape. This rectangle works four pineapple motifs side by side across a 185 cm width, with a chain-arch mesh between them. Yarn is lace-weight on a 2.75 mm hook. The pattern is adapted from Weldon's Practical Crochet (1886). Finished size is approximately 185 cm wide by 50 cm deep.
sourceNotes: Pineapple motif construction adapted from Weldon's Practical Crochet, Volume 3 (1887), 'Pineapple Crochet' and 'Shawl in Pineapple Stitch', Internet Archive. Double treble cluster fan arrangement updated for modern lace-weight yarn proportions.
heroPrompt: A rectangular lace crochet shawl with four vertical pineapple motifs in cream lace-weight yarn, spread flat on a dark wooden table, each pineapple fan clearly visible, photographed from directly above.

glossaryTerms.definition: A traditional crochet lace motif shaped like a tapered pineapple. It starts wide at the base with a fan of double trebles, then decreases by working progressively smaller clusters in each row until a single stitch closes the tip.
A tall stitch worked with three yarn-overs before inserting the hook, then drawing through pairs of loops four times. Double trebles form the fan at the base of each pineapple motif.
Two or more double trebles worked into the same space and joined at the top, used to decrease the width of the pineapple motif as it tapers toward the tip.

content.text: Pineapple crochet is one of the most recognisable Victorian lace patterns. Each
pineapple motif

begins with a wide fan of double trebles at the base, then tapers row by row through progressively smaller clusters until a single stitch closes the tip. This rectangular shawl places four pineapple motifs side by side with chain-arch mesh filling the spaces between them. The construction works from the wide base of the pineapples upward toward the tips, then returns to base level on the flip side to close each motif symmetrically.
A
double treble (dtr)

is wound three times before inserting the hook, then drawn through pairs of loops four times. The pineapple base fan is 9 dtr fanned into a single chain space. Each subsequent row pairs adjacent dtr into
dtr clusters
, reducing the count until one final dc closes the pineapple tip.

attrs.title: Materials
attrs.body: Approximately 350 g lace-weight yarn (approximately 800 m per 100 g). A 2.75 mm crochet hook (US C/2). Tapestry needle. Craft scissors. Stitch markers (8: 2 per pineapple, marking the base chain spaces). Blocking mat. Blocking pins (60 or more). Tape measure.

content.text: Gauge

One complete pineapple motif (base fan of 9 dtr to single dc tip) = approximately 45 cm long x 10 cm wide at the widest point, after blocking. The chain-arch mesh between motifs: 4 arch rows = 5 cm deep. Work a single pineapple swatch and block it before beginning the full shawl.
Stitches used
chain (ch): UK and US shared.
slip stitch (sl st): UK and US shared.
double crochet (dc): UK; the same move as US "single crochet" (sc).
treble (tr): UK; the same move as US "double crochet" (dc).
double treble (dtr): UK; the same move as US "treble crochet" (tr). Yarn over 3 times before inserting hook.
double treble cluster (dtr-cl): 2 dtr into the same space, joined at the top.
Pattern

The shawl is worked flat. The foundation chain runs the full 185 cm width. The pineapple motifs are established in rows 1 to 3, then taper through rows 4 to 12, with chain arches filling the spaces between motifs throughout. Four motifs sit at equal spacing across the width.
Foundation chain
Ch 277. Mark every 69th chain: these mark the centre chain of each pineapple base.
Row 1 (right side): establish pineapple bases

Ch 5 (counts as 1 dtr). Work 8 more dtr into the first marked chain (9 dtr fan, base of pineapple 1). *Ch 5, skip 8 ch, 1 dc in next ch, ch 5, skip 8 ch (mesh arch between motifs). 9 dtr into the next marked chain (base of next pineapple)*; repeat from * to * for remaining 3 pineapples. Ch 2, 1 tr in last ch to close. Turn. (4 pineapple fans of 9 dtr, separated by ch-5 arches)
Row 2

Ch 4 (counts as 1 dtr). Work [dtr-cl into same space as ch-4, ch 1] across the first pineapple fan, working a dtr-cl over each adjacent pair of dtr: 8 dtr-cl with ch-1 between each. *Ch 5, 1 dc into the mesh arch dc, ch 5. Work 8 dtr-cl with ch-1 between over next pineapple fan*; repeat across. Ch 2, 1 tr to close. Turn. (8 dtr-cl per pineapple, 4 pineapples)
Rows 3 to 11: taper each pineapple

On each subsequent row, pair adjacent dtr-cl from the row below into a new dtr-cl, reducing the cluster count by one on each side of the pineapple: row 3 has 7 dtr-cl, row 4 has 6, and so on down to row 11 with 1 dtr-cl. Between pineapples, the chain-arch mesh continues with ch 5 on each side of the mesh dc, increasing the arch length by 1 ch every two rows to keep the mesh proportional. The stitch count per pineapple reduces by 1 dtr-cl each row.
Row 12: close pineapple tips
Ch 4. *1 dc into the top of the single remaining dtr-cl (pineapple tip). Ch 7, 1 dc into mesh arch dc, ch 7*; repeat across. 1 tr to close. Turn. (4 closed pineapple tips)
Rows 13 to 16: mesh fill
Work 4 rows of ch-5 arch mesh across the full width to bring the shawl depth to 50 cm: *1 dc into arch, ch 5*; repeat across each row. Fasten off after row 16.
Finishing

Fasten off and weave in all ends through the solid parts of the mesh. Wet-block by soaking fully in cool water for 15 minutes, pressing gently, then pinning to 185 x 50 cm on a blocking mat. Pin each pineapple tip outward and pin the arch loops open. Leave until completely dry before unpinning.
Care
Handwash in cool water with mild wool wash. Do not wring or tumble-dry. Press excess water out in a towel and lay flat to dry, repinning the pineapple tips if needed.
What to try next

Work the same pineapple arrangement in a top-down triangle. Add one pineapple motif on each triangle increase row to grow the design. A single large pineapple motif worked as a standalone panel works well as a cushion cover centrepiece or a framed textile piece.
